status: development specification after preserved negative v4; not independent validation or preregistration
feature_source: exact v4 input matrices; no outcome-driven new columns or exclusions
anchor_transform: training-median/IQR asinh, monotone within a fitted model
feature_transform: training-median/IQR tanh, each feature in [-1,1]; zero-IQR fallback training std or 1
learner: greedy at most 2 distinct coordinates; per-coordinate bounded 1D optimization of near-anchor-pair weighted logistic loss plus ridge*coefficient squared/2
pair_weights: exp(-anchor_difference squared/2), normalized over training positive-negative pairs; protected ordering does not imply improved AUC
score: anchor + eta*tanh(sum of selected coefficient times transformed feature)
selection: choose stronger anchor on mean inner-fold AUC; score each correction by paired delta mean - 0.25*delta SD/sqrt(3) against that anchor; correction must improve at least 2/3 inner folds and risk score > 0.01; otherwise use anchor only; ties prefer earlier source, smaller eta, larger ridge, fewer steps
ungated_ablation: highest mean inner-fold AUC over the identical candidate menu, including two anchor-only candidates
static_ablation: same gated algorithm and candidate menu using only static v4 features
primary_metric: within-outer-fold AUC arithmetic mean then equal-weight cohort macro average; no fold-scale weakening of T
target: positive macro deltas over T and uHNDI at every seed, positive cohort mean deltas over both, and positive mean delta over anchor-selector ablation; all are development split stability only
historical_policy: read-only earlier results and code; new output directory results/sparse_increment_v5
fairness: all selection, transforms and sparse coordinate selection use training patients only; reuse v4 standard comparator predictions only after byte-identical feature and subject split validation; do not reuse v2 comparisons with different inputs
reporting: report every candidate family and adverse result; neither selecting strong anchors nor renaming a winning ablation alone establishes algorithm innovation
